material_systems.name: Solvent-Based MDF Edge Sealer

primer.notes: MUST be applied to MDF cut/routed edges BEFORE any latex product. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber swelling on MDF edges. This is step 1 of two-step MDF prime. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 2 and Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.3.

material_systems.notes: Edge-only application. Step 1 of MDF two-step prime process.

material_systems.name: High-Build Latex Face Primer for MDF

primer.notes: Applied to MDF face surfaces AFTER edge sealing with shellac/oil-based. Builds film, levels surface. Step 2 of two-step MDF prime.

material_systems.notes: Step 2 of MDF two-step prime. Face surfaces only — edges already sealed.

material_systems.name: Stain-Blocking Primer for Poplar

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Oil-Based Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for bare poplar. Green mineral streaks bleed through standard latex primers without stain-blocking. NOT optional. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Stain-blocking is not optional for poplar.

material_systems.name: Tannin-Blocking Primer for Hardwood

primer.notes: Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood (oak, cherry, walnut). Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Required for all bare hardwood substrates.

primer.notes: Standard primer-sealer to seal and provide tooth on plywood surfaces.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel

products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
finish.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Good for enclosed stairwells where yellowing is a concern. Same system as trim and window specs.

material_systems.notes: QT3 — satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel

products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
finish.notes: Superior flow and leveling. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away. Sands easily between coats. Same system as trim and window specs.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel

finish.coat_notes: QT5 brush/roll typically requires 3+ coats per FFD 15.10.3.
finish.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Same system as trim and window specs.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Stair riser/stringer primer coverage. Risers: EA count × riser SF each (~2.2 SF). Stringers: LF measurement (1 LF ≈ 1 SF per PDCA standard for linear trim). MDF edges may have different absorption rate.
assumptions: Single coat primer system (except MDF two-step)
Riser SF per unit ≈ 2.2 SF (3.5 ft wide × 0.625 ft high)

coverage_profiles.notes: Stair riser/stringer finish coverage on primed smooth surface. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush/roll has same per-coat coverage. Spray method: add 20-30% material waste for overspray in confined stairwell space.
assumptions: Stringer LF ≈ 1 SF per LF (standard trim width)

consumables.name: Ram Board Stair Armor tread protector
consumables.usage: Mandatory tread protection covering riser face bottom edge, tread surface, and bullnose
consumables.notes: Industry standard per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2. Spill Guard and Tread-Trac grip strips. One per tread. NEVER use plastic sheeting on treads — extreme fall hazard.

consumables.name: Low-tack safe-release masking tape
consumables.usage: Secure tread protection without damaging tread finish
consumables.notes: Low-tack prevents tread finish damage during protection removal.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer sanding for bare substrates, factory primer scuff
consumables.notes: 150 grit for initial bare wood/plywood sanding. Also for factory primer scuff.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer final sand, between-coat sanding (QT3 spot, QT4 full)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for final prep sand and between-coat sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD 15.4.1).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding. Mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5")
consumables.usage: Detail work for riser edges and stringer profiles
consumables.notes: 1.5-inch for detail edges. One per painter per material change.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush for riser face and stringer flat surfaces
consumables.notes: 2-2.5 inch for flat riser faces and stringer surfaces. One per painter.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for stair component spray finish
consumables.notes: Tight fan pattern for stair component work.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~30 risers or ~30 LF stringer. Use before every coat.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Wall masking along stringer edge, riser-to-tread edge masking

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.notes: Runner-style for landings. Required when floor_type = finished or partial.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.usage: Stringer-to-wall caulk and riser-to-stringer caulk joints
consumables.notes: One tube covers approximately 25 LF of caulk joint. Two joint types: stringer-to-wall (continuous) and riser-to-stringer (2 per riser × riser width).

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill fastener holes, minor defects on risers and stringers
consumables.notes: Lightweight or auto-body type depending on defect depth. One quart per ~50 risers.

consumables.name: Rosin paper (red or brown)
consumables.usage: Alternative/supplemental tread protection under Ram Board
consumables.notes: Optional additional layer under Stair Armor for premium protection.

stair_tread_covers.description: Mandatory tread protection from Day 1 through cleanup
stair_tread_covers.condition: ALWAYS — mandatory regardless of method. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners at landing areas

wall_adjacent.description: Wall masking along stringer top edge when spraying

compatibility_rules.description: All finish systems are compatible with all primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer and finish are independent selections. All combinations valid.

compatibility_rules.description: SS_PRIMED_FACTORY compatible with all finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. No additional primer needed.

compatibility_rules.description: MDF two-step prime: shellac edge seal MUST precede latex face prime
compatibility_rules.notes: SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC on edges first, then SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX on faces. Never reverse.

risk_notes.risk: Irreversible fiber swelling if water-based product contacts raw MDF cut edges
risk_notes.mitigation: Always seal MDF edges with shellac/oil-based sealer (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC) before any latex product.

risk_notes.risk: Green mineral streaks bleed through non-stain-blocking primer
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK. Stain-blocking is MANDATORY for bare poplar.

risk_notes.risk: Drips, spills, or foot traffic damage on unprotected treads
risk_notes.mitigation: Ram Board Stair Armor from Day 1. Never use plastic sheeting — fall hazard.

risk_notes.risk: Oil-modified products yellow in UV-deprived environments
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (non-yellowing 100% acrylic) for basement/enclosed stairwells.

material_notes.dual_system_architecture: TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven with 5 distinct paths. (2) Finish systems are QT-driven. Any primer can pair with any finish.
material_notes.mdf_two_step_note: MDF requires two-step prime: edge seal with shellac/oil-based (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC), then face prime with latex (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX). Order is mandatory.
material_notes.coverage_note: Risers: EA × ~2.2 SF per riser. Stringers: LF × ~1 SF per LF. Total SF for coverage calculation.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS data, aligned with trim/window spec coverage

assumptions.value: ~2.2 SF per riser (3.5 ft wide × 0.625 ft high)
